headline_marked: Sarjis Alam says [[no one will be allowed to become another Sheikh Hasina]] in future Bangladesh
headline: Sarjis Alam says no one will be allowed to become another Sheikh Hasina in future Bangladesh
summary: The NCP Northern Region Chief Coordinator warned against blind loyalty to political parties and urged law enforcement to regain their professional honor.
details: Sarjis Alam, the Northern Region Chief Coordinator of the National Citizens Party (NCP), stated that Bangladesh will not allow any new leader to replicate the style of Sheikh Hasina's rule.
Speaking at a road meeting in Kalihati, Tangail, he criticized the previous administration's tendency to portray the leader as 'good' while everyone else was 'bad'.
Addressing Tarique Rahman, he emphasized that leaders must take responsibility for the actions of their party workers, including extortion, syndicates, and drug trafficking.
He urged the public not to sell or mortgage their conscience to any political party or symbol, warning that blind support prevents real change in the country.
Sarjis also called upon the police and other law enforcement agencies to restore their honor and dignity through professional conduct.
He claimed that the police force was misused by Sheikh Hasina to maintain her power before the July uprising.
The event in Tangail was attended by several NCP leaders, including Joint Convener and MP Atiqur Rahman Mujahid and Sorwar Tushar.
caption:

He urged the public not to sell or mortgage their conscience to any political party or symbol, warning that blind support prevents real change in the country.

Sarjis also called upon the police and other law enforcement agencies to restore their honor and dignity through professional conduct.

He claimed that the police force was misused by Sheikh Hasina to maintain her power before the July uprising.

The event in Tangail was attended by several NCP leaders, including Joint Convener and MP Atiqur Rahman Mujahid and Sorwar Tushar.

headline: PM Tareq Rahman: Teachers' salaries to be increased gradually
summary: The Prime Minister announced that primary and secondary school teachers will see a phased increase in their pay to ensure they can focus on students without needing second jobs.
details: Prime Minister Tareq Rahman informed Parliament on Wednesday that the government will gradually increase the salaries of primary and secondary school teachers across the country.
caption:
No more second jobs for teachers? PM Tareq Rahman promises a phased salary hike for primary and secondary educators.

Prime Minister Tareq Rahman informed Parliament on Wednesday that the government will gradually increase the salaries of primary and secondary school teachers across the country.
